*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and
the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
Council Meeting of June 15, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l  The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the
  conference 5 minutes prior.
  l  If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from
  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l  If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone
  line, it is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone
  transmission. Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be
  inaudible due to feedback.
  l  Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes
  detailed below for the respective City Council Dates:

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting;
however, members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access
options 1 and 2 noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in
appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of
the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and
regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-
related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or
offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or
service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at
310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA
90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org
no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  June 15, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  June 15, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint
  Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority
  Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/ Joint Powers Authority Member
  Dotson.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
  personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.
  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 3,
  Letter from the City Attorney’s Office returning a late claim, and 5, Amendment No. 1 to
  Agreement No. 21-005 with HHJ Construction, Inc., to complete the residential sound
  insulation work.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 2,
  Approval of the Minutes of the Meeting held on November 24, 2020, and H-SPH-1,
  Setting of a public hearing to consider the Inglewood Housing Authority 1-Year (2021-
  2022) Agency Plan and related certifications.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June
  10, 2021, in the amount of $850,489.06 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor
  Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman / Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes:  None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/ Housing Authority Member
  Dotson.

  MINUTES.  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
   June 15, 2021

  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on November 24, 2020,
  be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None;
  Abstain: Council Member Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Return Late Claim Pursuant to Government Code Section 911.2:
  1) Ta’Jhauna Robinson for alleged tire damage; rod obstruction on June 14, 2020.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Dotson that
  City Council does hereby return late claim listed as A-1. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 21–175 APPROVED - PETE MORAGA; PAYMENT OF
  OUTSTANDING INVOICES AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated June 15, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of a three-year agreement (with the option to extend
  two additional one-year terms) with Pete Moraga to provide Bilingual (Spanish)
  Translation, Community Engagement and Outreach Services for the City of Inglewood.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-175 in the annual
  amount of $94,000 (total amount of $282,000); and 2) Authorize the payment of
  outstanding invoices submitted in the amount of $10,350. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

103.3  AMENDMENT  NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 21–005 APPROVED - HHJ
  CONSTRUCTION, INC APPROVED: PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – HHJ
  CONSTRUCTION, INC.  Staff report dated June 15, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 21-005 with HHJ
  Construction, Inc., extending the term to October 29, 2021 to complete the residential
  sound insulation work on the remaining residential units of Project Phase XV, Group
  22A.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 21-
  005; and 2) Authorized payment of an outstanding invoice in the amount of $445,106.36.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  PUBLIC HEARING SET. Staff report dated June 15, 2021, was presented requesting
  that a public hearing be set to receive public comments regarding the City’s 2020 Urban
  Management Plan (UWMP).

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for June 29, 2021, at 2:00 p.m.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson spoke on the celebration
  of Juneteenth with a quote from President Barack Obama. She also wished all fathers a
  Happy Father’s Day, and ended her report by reading quotes that honored fathers.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
 June 15, 2021

  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on continuous and ongoing Brown Act Violations,
  specifically the time limits allowed to speak on Agenda Items. In addition, she also
  requested respect, transparency, and a meeting with the Council.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills, and requested an Election
  schedule for the Council.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts wished Marla Gibbs happy
  birthday and adjourned the meeting at the hour of 2:27 p.m.

  Approved this ______ day of _______, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
